A_extra.issue: Give processing steps from raw data to figures, with a data and code statement
Disclose full parameter ranges measured (gate beyond ±50 V, other LED drives, frequencies below 0.1 Hz) and why the shown ranges were chosen
Dielectric loss peaks may be Maxwell-Wagner relaxations from contacts or internal interfaces; measure a bare KTaO3(111) substrate and repeat the loss scan after illumination
Warm up at zero gate after cycling to see where the imprinted state resets (trap release steps)
The 35 K and 95 K traces in Fig. 4a are noisier than neighbours and each maximum in Fig. 4b rests on one point; repeat at nearby temperatures
Superconducting layer thickness not tracked across gate and light states

B_extra.issue: Dielectric capacitor is the full 0.5 mm substrate, so epsilon and tan delta probe bulk KTaO3, not the interfacial region
Loss peaks could be off-centre impurity dipoles (Li) or Maxwell-Wagner/space-charge relaxations; control with metal electrodes and no 2DEG, plus thickness dependence
5 V excitation (~100 V/cm) may be outside linear response and may disturb the imprinted state; show amplitude independence
Epsilon saturating near 2300 is below bulk KTaO3 values, suggesting effective area or thickness differs from nominal
Delta_L versus epsilon linearity is nearly automatic since induced charge scales with epsilon; compare at fixed induced charge or against integrated gate charge
Demonstrate switching between zero-resistance and resistive states at a fixed temperature inside the transition; report onset, zero-resistance and width per state
Photon energy exceeding Ea is not a valid argument that 1.97 eV light couples to dipole reorientation; give a calibrated flux and show the illuminated state is saturated at each temperature
Non-monotonic tau(T) and short fitting window (~2 tau) make Delta_R and tau strongly correlated; show fit uncertainties and finer temperature steps
Non-superconducting (001) KTaO3 reference interface to isolate effects specific to the (111) superconductor
Single-carrier Hall analysis questionable for multiband KTaO3(111); show Hall curves and test nonlinearity
Hall Delta n has the opposite sign to simple field-effect doping; integrate the gate-current transient for charge bookkeeping
Supp. Fig. 3a gate current was measured after illumination but used to explain the pristine drift; show the first-ever sweep
Type B vs Type A Rs difference (856 vs 840 Ohm) follows from ending on opposite loop branches and is about twice Delta_L at 10 K
Rs and n values inconsistent across figures of presumably the same device; state cooldown and history of each dataset
